lessons.name: F&P Robotics
lessons.summary: F&P Robotics builds collaborative arms and mobile robots that combine moving, handling objects, and interacting with people.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

F&P Robotics builds collaborative arms and mobile robots that combine moving, handling objects, and interacting with people.

![F&P Sola mobile robot with its arm, gripper, screen and wheeled base labelled](/img/lessons/orgs_corporate_2-fp-robotics.webp)
*Sola combines a mobile base with an arm. Source: [F&P Robotics](https://www.fp-robotics.com/solutions/mobile-robot/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Mobile manipulation** means moving around and handling objects: Sola targets laboratory workflows, while Lio also supports service and interaction tasks.
- **The myP interface** offers browser-based block programming and Python development; an API is a software interface for connecting other applications.
- **A concrete workflow:** Sola transports laboratory samples and uses its arm to move them between instruments and delivery points.

> **Key idea:** A useful mobile robot must coordinate its base, arm, and surrounding workflow, not merely demonstrate each separately.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think service orchestration:** navigation and manipulation resemble separate services; a successful delivery needs their results in the correct order.
- **Connect Lio and Sola** in the map: compare a person-facing assistance task with a laboratory transport task.
- **Our exercise:** sketch a sample-delivery state machine with pickup, travel, handover, and failure states before attempting a physical demonstration.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the technology demonstrations** to see how the programming interface connects actions rather than assuming a language model controls everything.
2. **Prepare a narrow question:** ask how a failed pickup is detected and communicated to the workflow.
3. **Use the public contact form** to propose an engineering discussion; the published partnership offering concerns technology integration, not a promised student sponsorship.

lessons.name: FabLab Bern (89grad project)
lessons.summary: FabLab Bern is a digital-fabrication workshop, described as a project of 89grad GmbH, where people turn designs into physical objects.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

FabLab Bern is a digital-fabrication workshop, described as a project of 89grad GmbH, where people turn designs into physical objects.

![Exterior of the building pictured on FabLab Bern's contact page](/img/lessons/orgs_corporate_2-fablab-bern.webp)
*The workshop's contact page shows its building. Source: [FabLab Bern](https://fablab-bern.ch/kontakt/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Fabrication means making parts:** the workshop lists 3D printers, a laser cutter, lathes, and computer-controlled milling machines that cut material.
- **Electronics tools** include soldering irons and an oscilloscope, an instrument for displaying electrical signals over time.
- **It is not a robot vendor:** the useful connection is prototyping parts and learning tools, rather than buying a complete robotic platform.

> **Key idea:** A makerspace fills the gap between a design file and a part you can actually fit to a robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of fabrication as compilation:** a digital design becomes a physical artifact, but fit and material must also be checked.
- **Connect Intro: CAD and 3D-print a robot part:** CAD means computer-aided design; a camera bracket is a concrete first design exercise.
- **A small worked example:** design a bracket, fabricate it, check its fit, then revise the model; keep each revision like a software release.

## How to engage

1. **Read the machine-specific course requirements:** introductory training is required before using the corresponding equipment independently.
2. **Contact the workshop publicly** with a drawing and material question; confirm access conditions and fees before planning travel from Paris.
3. **Propose a modest prototype** rather than a whole robot; the course overview and team-event page explain supported learning formats.

lessons.name: FANUC
lessons.summary: FANUC supplies factory automation, including industrial robot arms, collaborative CRX robots, and software for programming robots before installation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

FANUC supplies factory automation, including industrial robot arms, collaborative CRX robots, and software for programming robots before installation.

![White and green FANUC CRX-10iA collaborative robot arm](/img/lessons/orgs_corporate_2-fanuc.webp)
*A CRX-10iA collaborative arm. Source: [FANUC](https://www.fanuc.eu/eu-en/crx-series), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **FANUC CRX series** arms can be hand-guided to positions and programmed through a tablet interface with drag-and-drop actions.
- **One concrete model:** the CRX-10iA has six axes, a 10 kg payload, and 1,249 mm reach; payload is the load the robot carries.
- **FANUC ROBOGUIDE** simulates robot cells, meaning the arm, surrounding equipment, and programmed task, before the physical installation.

> **Key idea:** Industrial robotics is about a repeatable production process, not just making an arm move once.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think staging before production:** offline programming tests a virtual workcell before transferring a program to the real controller.
- **A worked planning exercise:** sketch a machine-loading cell, choose pickup and placement positions, and list obstacles that the virtual robot must avoid.
- **Compare toolchains:** distinguish hand-guided teaching from learning a behavior from recorded demonstrations; both can involve a person moving an arm.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the CRX demonstration** and identify the arm, tablet, and end effector, the tool attached to the arm's tip.
2. **Explore Academy training** and ask the French training center about suitable introductory or education sessions through public channels.
3. **Ask about ROBOGUIDE access** before budgeting a simulation project; do not assume commercial software is freely available.

> **Watch out:** A collaborative arm still needs an application-specific safety assessment, especially when carrying tools or parts.

lessons.name: FAULHABER SA (Swiss operations)
lessons.summary: FAULHABER SA is the group's Swiss operation, developing and producing compact motors, gearheads, and linear drives used in precision equipment and robotics.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

FAULHABER SA is the group's Swiss operation, developing and producing compact motors, gearheads, and linear drives used in precision equipment and robotics.

![FAULHABER's Croglio site with its factory buildings and surrounding hills](/img/lessons/orgs_corporate_2-faulhaber.webp)
*The Croglio site in Switzerland. Source: [FAULHABER](https://www.faulhaber.com/en/about-us/locations/faulhaber-sa-ch/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Croglio develops and manufactures drives:** the Swiss operation also has branches in Grenchen and Bioggio producing mainly metal geared parts.
- **A gearhead** changes the motor's speed and turning force; a linear drive produces straight-line movement instead of rotation.
- **An encoder** measures motion or position, letting a controller compare the requested movement with what actually happened.

> **Key idea:** A robot joint is a combination of motor, transmission, sensing, and control, not simply a motor with software attached.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think modular dependencies:** motor, gearhead, and encoder must be compatible, just as software packages need matching interfaces.
- **A concrete selection exercise:** describe a small gripper's required turning force, speed, and available space before choosing any components.
- **Connect Actuator sizing: torque, inertia and thermal duty:** torque means turning force; a drive choice starts with the load, not an impressive motor photograph.

## How to engage

1. **Watch FAULHABER Drive Time** for a component-selection explanation before reading a detailed product table.
2. **Compare the gearhead and encoder references:** write down which part changes motion and which part measures it.
3. **Use the Swiss public contact** with an application sketch and requirements; ask about selection guidance or an educational explanation, not an unspecified sponsorship.

lessons.name: Festo
lessons.summary: Festo supplies pneumatic and electric automation technology, technical education systems, and research demonstrators inspired by living things.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Festo supplies pneumatic and electric automation technology, technical education systems, and research demonstrators inspired by living things.

![Festo BionicMobileAssistant with its robotic arm above a ball-shaped mobile base](/img/lessons/orgs_corporate_2-festo.webp)
*BionicMobileAssistant balances on a ball. Source: [Festo press](https://press.festo.com/en/node/3199), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Pneumatic actuation** uses compressed air to create movement; Festo also supplies electrically driven motion systems and automation software.
- **Festo Didactic** provides technical learning systems, making the education business distinct from components installed in factory machines.
- **BionicMobileAssistant is a research prototype:** it combines a mobile base, electric arm, and pneumatic BionicSoftHand 2.0 developed with ETH Zurich.

> **Key idea:** Festo's animal- and plant-inspired demonstrations explore mechanisms; they are not a catalogue of ready-made general-purpose robots.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think hardware abstraction:** software requests a motion, but an air-powered hand and an electric joint require different physical interfaces.
- **A concrete example:** the Bionic Flower uses a stepper motor to open and close petals, with sensors reacting to touch, proximity, or light.
- **Connect Soft pneumatic actuators and compliant-body fabrication:** compliant means yielding rather than remaining rigid; study why the mechanism changes the control problem.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the mobile-assistant video** and separate its three subsystems before focusing on the AI.
2. **Read the original prototype release** to distinguish demonstrated capabilities from possible future applications mentioned in the text.
3. **Explore the education material** and propose a small sensing-to-motion exercise; use public Festo channels for training or technical questions rather than assuming prototype availability.

lessons.name: Franka Robotics
lessons.summary: Franka Robotics develops force-sensitive robot arms and developer interfaces for robotics and AI research.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Franka Robotics develops force-sensitive robot arms and developer interfaces for robotics and AI research.

![Close-up of a white Franka Research 3 robot's joints and metal tool mounting flange](/img/lessons/orgs_corporate_2-franka.webp)
*Franka Research 3 hardware. Source: [Franka Robotics](https://franka.de/franka-research-3), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Franka Research 3 (FR3)** has seven movable joints, seven torque sensors, a 3 kg payload, and an 855 mm reach.
- **Torque sensors** measure turning force at the joints, helping estimate contact with objects and supporting force-sensitive experiments.
- **The libfranka library is an open-source C++ interface:** the Franka Control Interface can exchange commands and measurements at 1 kHz, meaning 1,000 times per second.

> **Key idea:** Access to measured forces and low-level commands makes an arm a research instrument, not just an automated task player.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an API with deadlines:** a control callback must deliver commands on time; a real-time loop is not an ordinary web request.
- **A worked timing example:** 1,000 updates per second leaves one millisecond per update; separate expensive model inference from that fast loop.
- **Connect Feedback control & PID:** compare desired and measured motion before exploring learned behaviors; the arm's sensors expose what actually happens.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the FR3 product demonstration** and distinguish its arm, gripper, and external control computer.
2. **Read FCI requirements and compatibility guidance** before treating a research paper's code as a runnable hardware setup.
3. **Inspect libfranka examples** and use public community discussions for reproducible technical questions; include robot and software versions.

> **Watch out:** Low-level FCI control requires custom operator-protection rules; internal supervision does not replace application safety.

lessons.name: Geek+
lessons.summary: Geek+ builds warehouse robots and coordination software that bring stored goods to people instead of making people walk to every shelf.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Geek+ builds warehouse robots and coordination software that bring stored goods to people instead of making people walk to every shelf.

![Published Geekplus visualization of a warehouse storage and picking layout](/img/lessons/orgs_corporate_2-geekplus.webp)
*Shelf-to-Person warehouse layout visualization. Source: [Geekplus](https://www.geekplus.com/solutions/shelf-to-person), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Shelf-to-Person** uses mobile robots to bring entire shelves to operators; the person picks the needed items at a workstation.
- **PopPick adds automated tote delivery:** a tote is a storage container, retrieved from shelving and presented for picking.
- **The software divides responsibilities:** RMS schedules robots, WES manages task logic, and G-Studio supports simulation of the warehouse system.

> **Key idea:** Warehouse automation succeeds when the whole flow of goods works, not when a single robot drives impressively.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think distributed task queues:** orders create work, robots execute transport jobs, and shared routes and stations are limited resources.
- **Connect Geek+ warehouse AMRs:** AMR means autonomous mobile robot; study how a fleet differs from one vehicle following a route.
- **A worked paper exercise:** give two simulated robots three shelf-delivery jobs and one station; compare completion order and waiting time, not only driving speed.

## How to engage

1. **Watch Shelf-to-Person operation** and identify what moves: shelves, containers, robots, and people play different roles.
2. **Compare the robot families** with the software overview; separate warehouse workflow coordination from each robot's local movement.
3. **Use the public inquiry channel** with a fleet-scheduling question or a clearly scoped student simulation; do not assume the commercial fleet software is open source.
